key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can uniquely fingerprint and quantify specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films, turning defect diagnosis into a direct spectroscopic measurement.
engineering_relevance: This enables non-contact, room-temperature quality control and passivation guidance for perovskite solar-cell manufacturing, helping reduce recombination losses and improve efficiency.
method: Measured THz spectra (0.3–3.0 THz) of SVE-fabricated MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3 thin films.
Matched intrinsic phonon modes and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrations to build material-specific THz fingerprints.
Used oscillator-strength analysis to link the 1.58 THz MAPbI3 absorption to CH3NH2 defect concentration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a linear relationship between the 1.58 THz absorption oscillator strength and XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting quantitative defect metrology.
watch_item: The approach depends on building reliable composition-specific THz fingerprint libraries and may require careful interpretation when multiple defect species overlap spectrally.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
